markdown_content: ## Overview of Render Light Naming in CLO 2025 This section explains the new feature in CLO 2025 that allows users to name render lights within the software. Naming lights improves workflow management by making it easier to identify, organize, and control multiple light sources in 3D garment rendering. --- ## Accessing the Render Window and Setting Up Views To start working with render lights, open the render window by selecting **Render > Render** from the top toolbar. Users typically set up their preferred camera angle and lighting in the 3D window first. After adjusting the view, click the **lock camera** button to fix the camera position for rendering. To save a custom camera view: - Right-click in an empty area of the 3D window (avoid clicking on the avatar or garment). - Select **Custom View**. - Click the camera icon to capture and save the current view. Locking the camera ensures that the render view updates interactively while maintaining the chosen angle. --- ## Managing Multiple Lights in CLO When working with complex lighting setups, it’s important to keep track of each light source. In CLO’s render toolbar, a **light icon** provides access to all scene lights. This panel allows users to: - View all lights active in the scene. - Control whether each light is visible in the 3D window or active in the render. - Toggle lights on or off in real-time using **interactive render** mode. Lights have two states: - **Show 3D**: Controls visibility in the 3D workspace. - **Activate**: Controls whether the light affects the render output. This dual control allows for precise adjustments without deleting lights. --- ## Naming Lights for Better Workflow Organization By default, lights are generically named (e.g., Directional Light, Rectangle Light, IES Light), which can make complex scenes difficult to manage. CLO 2025 allows users to rename lights directly in the light panel: - Double-click the name field of the light. - Enter a descriptive name, such as "Orange," "Water Reflected," or "Sunset Glow." - Press Enter or click away to save the new name. Naming lights clarifies their purpose and placement, making it easier to identify each light’s role in the scene. This is especially useful when adjusting specific lights, such as toggling reflections or adjusting intensities. --- ## Practical Uses of Named Lights Named lights enable users to: - Quickly identify and activate or deactivate specific lights to test different lighting effects. - Understand the function of each light in the context of the scene (e.g., "Water Reflected" for reflection effects). - Control lighting more intuitively during interactive rendering. For example, turning off the "Water Reflected" light shows how the scene looks without reflection, helping to decide if the effect should be kept. --- ## Saving and Reusing Light Setups Users can save their entire lighting setup, including all named lights, by clicking **Save** in the render toolbar. These saved configurations can be imported into other projects using the **Open** function, allowing for consistent lighting across multiple files and efficient reuse of complex setups. --- ## Summary CLO 2025’s render light naming feature enhances lighting workflow by: - Allowing customizable names for each light. - Providing easy toggling and visibility control in both 3D and render windows. - Enabling saving and reuse of lighting setups across projects. - Improving scene organization and lighting experimentation through descriptive naming. This feature is particularly valuable for complex scenes with multiple lights tailored to specific moods or effects, such as a beach sunset with directional sun and soft ambient lighting.
